name: Westmere Residential Energy Performance Act

source_sentences: K1, the performance standard: new homes whose DEI exceeds a maximum may not be built.
The standard covers new residential buildings of three stories or fewer above grade, including homes rebuilt after demolition, and it binds builders and owners who apply for a building permit.
The existing homes of the state are not covered by it.
On 1 January of each later year the maximum falls by 4% of the Year 1 value.
Renovations and alterations of existing homes are exempt.
Manufactured homes built to the national standard are exempt.
A certificate of occupancy requires a rater's certificate.
The Energy Office audits 2% of certificates.
The Energy Office's audit unit is funded by a new general-fund appropriation.

unclear.text: The Act requires the Energy Office to adjust the index for dwelling size, but it does not say what the adjustment is.
readings: U1-a: no adjustment beyond the per-square-foot measure
U1-b: homes above 2,500 square feet are held to the maximum as if they were 2,500 square feet

unclear.text: The Act does not say which code the rebate's "applicable state energy code" means for a home vested under K2.
readings: U2-a: the code in force on the filing date
U2-b: the code in force when the rebate is claimed at completion

context: The State Energy Office's records show that the median DEI of new homes has fallen by about 1.5% a year for ten years without any state code, as heat pumps became cheaper, buyers asked for efficient homes, and the utilities' rebate program paid for homes that beat its baseline.
The Halden metropolitan area, with about a quarter of the state's new building, straddles the state line with the neighboring state of Brennick, which has no comparable code.
